skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate, edit, upscale, and stitch AI images through the inference.sh belt CLI. The skill documents model choices and workflows for GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, P-Image, ImagineArt, and Topaz.
skill.summary: Use inference.sh belt commands to generate, edit, upscale, and stitch AI images with hosted models.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only, but it authorizes and instructs use of the external belt CLI. Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting or model IDs, while command examples and install commands are real external command guidance. No prompt injection text was found, but prompts and image inputs may be sent to third-party services.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to documented belt commands, or require confirmation before login, install, or account-changing operations.
Add a clear privacy notice that prompts, uploaded images, and image URLs are sent to inference.sh and model providers.
Replace the remote Markdown image with a local asset or remove it to avoid automatic third-party fetches.
Separate related-skill installs from the main workflow and tell users to review packages before running npx skills add.

content.user_title: Generate AI Images with Hosted Models
content.value_statement: Image teams need repeatable ways to choose models and prepare prompts for hosted generation. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for using inference.sh image apps.
actual_capabilities: Lists hosted image models, including GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, P-Image, ImagineArt, and Topaz.
Shows workflows for text-to-image, image editing, image upscaling, and image stitching.
Provides example prompt fields for quality settings, aspect ratios, image URLs, and text rendering.
Directs users to the inference.sh image app store for more model options.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running hosted apps through the belt CLI.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an account that can access hosted image apps.
Sends prompts, image URLs, and selected inputs to external model providers.
Does not include local image generation models or offline rendering instructions.
Model availability, pricing, and output quality can change outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Create Marketing Visuals
use_cases.description: Plan product shots, social graphics, and campaign concepts using hosted image generation models.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Generate quick visual directions for packaging, apparel, hardware, and interface presentation images.

use_cases.title: Explore Model Options
use_cases.description: Compare image model choices for editing, text rendering, upscaling, and cinematic generation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-image-generation skill to create an image prompt for [subject] in [style]. Recommend one beginner-friendly model.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Product Mockup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to plan a product mockup for [product]. Include lighting, background, composition, and the best model choice.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to revise an existing image. Change [element] to [new direction] while preserving the main subject.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Advanced Model Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to compare three model workflows for [goal]. Include tradeoffs for quality, speed, editing, and text rendering.

output_examples.input: A designer needs a studio product image for a ceramic coffee mug.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a product-focused model, refines the prompt, suggests studio lighting, and identifies the belt workflow to run.

output_examples.input: A marketer wants to change an existing product photo background to a sunset beach.
output_examples.output: The skill selects an editing workflow, frames the background change clearly, and notes that the source image URL is sent externally.

output_examples.input: A creative developer needs to upscale a generated concept image.
output_examples.output: The skill points to the Topaz upscaling workflow and explains when to use it after generation.

best_practices: Use clear subject, setting, style, lighting, and aspect ratio details in each prompt.
Review model capabilities before choosing between generation, editing, upscaling, and stitching workflows.
Avoid sending sensitive prompts, private image URLs, or unpublished assets to external providers.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every listed model supports the same fields, quality levels, or editing features.
Do not paste confidential client images or private URLs without approval.
Do not run optional install commands without reviewing the external skill or package first.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps choose hosted image models and prepare belt CLI workflows for generation, editing, upscaling, and stitching.

faq.question: Does it generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses inference.sh hosted apps through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for image editing workflows that reference source image URLs.

faq.question: What should I avoid sending?
faq.answer: Avoid private images, confidential prompts, restricted brand assets, and sensitive image URLs.

faq.question: Why does it require belt?
faq.answer: The documented workflows run inference.sh apps through the belt command line interface.
